RELIEF NULL: the official report states no dollar figures. The Senate letter (Durbin et al., Feb 26, 2026) says '13 enforcement actions, obtaining less than $10 million in relief' and cites no source. Secondary slides (Gibson Dunn, Feb 2026; FIA, Apr 2026) put total relief at 'less than $1 billion', with 'less than $10 million' from actions filed by the current administration. So the Senate '<$10M' appears to be that narrower measure and is not comparable with prior totals, which count all orders entered in the year, including in earlier-filed cases (e.g., 2025 default judgments in Yukom, $338.7M CMP + $112.9M restitution, and Agridime, $102.9M restitution, per Paul Weiss). Other counts: Gibson Dunn's slide says 11 actions; Sen. Reed (Apr 24, 2026) says the CFTC website shows 'one new enforcement action in 2025'. That is a calendar-year count on a different basis and cannot be reconciled with the report. Staffing: Durbin letter says Division staffing fell 'at least 25 percent' and the Chicago office went from 20 enforcement attorneys to none (as reported). FIA cites a 20% CFTC-wide staff reduction. No exact FY2025 headcount.
